PullRequest.Title: Fix customization modal title when Cloud harness is selected
PullRequest.Body: This pull request addresses the issue with the Cloud harness customizations modal title not rendering correctly. The changes made include: - Updated the `SessionsAICustomizationWorkspaceService` to utilize the repository-facing workspace label for Cloud workspaces, ensuring the title follows the format `Cloud · `. - Local and worktree harnesses will continue to use the folder name for their titles. - Added a regression test in `aiCustomizationWorkspaceService.test.ts` to cover the new title formatting. Validation steps have been performed, and both the transpilation and targeted unit tests have passed successfully.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agent Customizations modal for an active Cloud/virtual session workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The delayed workspace service derives activeProjectLabel from activeSession -> activeChat -> workspace, selects workspace.label for a virtual workspace, and the open-editor action copies that string into the singleton editor input before editorService.openEditor. The label read is synchronous and on the modal-open critical path; all existing editor creation and rendering work is unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one active session, one active chat, and one workspace are read. The changed branch accesses scalar fields and does not enumerate workspace folders or customizations, so work remains O(1) regardless of repository size or folder count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous derived-observable evaluation per initial demand or invalidation; editor input updates are equality-deduplicated by setTargetLabels. No queue, parallel fan-out, or asynchronous work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The derived observable retains its normal cached value/dependency behavior. The diff changes only the selected scalar value for virtual workspaces and neither adds a cache nor changes cold/warm execution behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing the changed derivation through the modal open action and editor input: no filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, network, serialization payload, collection copy, or layout read/write is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful magnitude uncertainty: the added isVirtualWorkspace check and alternate string property read are constant-time in-memory operations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Before the diff, modal opening read folders[0].name; after it, virtual workspaces read workspace.label while non-virtual workspaces retain the prior read. Frequency, cardinality, allocation shape, and downstream rendering behavior are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change the active session/workspace while the customization editor exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The activeProjectLabel derived observable is invalidated by the existing active-session/chat/workspace dependencies; the editor's existing autorun calls updateTargetLabelPresentation, which updates the input label only when the string differs. The diff adds no new subscription, autorun, or rendering stage.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active workspace transition triggers one constant-time branch and scalar read; effective cardinality is one workspace, not the number of folders, sessions, or customization items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable propagation on the UI path, with no introduced asynchronous tasks or concurrent operations. Existing string equality in setTargetLabels coalesces unchanged labels.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing observable invalidation and equality behavior remains intact. There are no positive/negative cache states or remote cache misses on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the service derivation, editor autorun, updateTargetLabelPresentation, and setTargetLabels implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session-switch frequency varies by user, but each changed evaluation is bounded O(1) and introduces no expensive resource use.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR changes only which already-resident string is returned for virtual workspaces; it does not increase update frequency, force layout, serialize the label, or retain additional workspace state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced both modal-open and reactive workspace-change paths. The single production change adds a constant-time boolean branch and scalar string read, preserving observable caching, update cardinality, and all expensive-boundary behavior. No actionable performance finding or qualifying regression-fix learning signal was found.
